root_idea.summary: The root centers on emergence into view and strength expressed through the back: what becomes outward, elevated, dominant, or relied upon.
root_idea.development: The semantic field develops from the human back as the outward and supporting side. From this arise meanings of appearing, becoming manifest, rising above or overcoming, supporting another, carrying burdens, and putting something behind one's back.

senses.definition: To emerge into visibility or become apparent, manifest, or prevalent.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for something becoming perceptible after being hidden; with a condition such as فساد, it can mean becoming widespread or manifest.

senses.definition: To prevail over, overcome, or gain mastery of someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with عَلَى; the object may be an opponent, a thing to be overcome, or a structure to be surmounted.

senses.definition: To come to know, become acquainted with, or gain awareness of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially with عَلَى; in the Quran this includes attaining awareness of private matters and discovering or recognizing people.

senses.definition: To mount, climb onto, or get upon the top or back of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a physical object such as a wall, mountain, or other elevated structure.

senses.definition: To aid, assist, support, or back someone, including by aiding one side against another.
senses.usage_conditions: The reciprocal or opposing-party construction can express support for one another or support against an adversary.

senses.definition: To pronounce the formula of ẓihār: to declare one's wife to be to oneself like the back of one's mother, thereby treating marital relations as forbidden.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional pre-Islamic repudiation formula, Quranically discussed in the construction ظَاهَرَ مِنِ امْرَأَتِهِ and its variant readings.

senses.definition: To make apparent, show, manifest, disclose, or reveal something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used causatively for bringing something hidden or unexpressed into view or public awareness.

senses.definition: To make something prevail, dominant, or victorious over another.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, especially with a religion or doctrine as object, the causative sense can be realized as granting ascendancy rather than merely making visible.

senses.definition: To enter or be present at the time of noon.
senses.usage_conditions: A temporal use of the Form IV verb, equivalent to entering the time called ظُهْر or ظَهِيرَة.

senses.definition: To support or aid one another; to combine in support of a cause or party.
senses.usage_conditions: The reciprocal Form VI expresses mutual assistance and may be construed against an opposing party.

senses.definition: Outward, external, apparent, visible, or manifest.
senses.usage_conditions: Contrasted with باطن; it can describe perceptible reality, the outward side of something, or what is evident rather than hidden.
Used of a person or group having mastery, and in the divine name الظاهر, of the One who is ascendant over all things.
The feminine active-participle form describes something outwardly evident or accessible to perception.

senses.definition: An aider, assistant, helper, or supporter.
senses.usage_conditions: It may be singular or collective in sense and is commonly construed with عَلَى to express support against an opponent.

senses.definition: The back, the bodily part opposite the belly.
senses.usage_conditions: Used literally of human beings and animals, and in Quranic expressions for something borne on or placed behind the back.

senses.definition: The upper, outer, or exterior surface or side of something.
senses.usage_conditions: This includes the exposed surface of the earth or another object, contrasted with its interior or underside.

senses.definition: Put behind one's back and consequently ignored, neglected, or disregarded.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative relational formation used for something to which one turns one's back, abandons, or pays no attention.

senses.definition: Noon, midday, or the period of intense midday heat.
senses.usage_conditions: The exact limits vary by usage: it may denote the point of midday, the time after the sun's decline, or the vehement heat around midday, especially in summer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go out to the outside of a place.
Of a bird, to migrate or move from one region to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported especially of a vulture moving toward Najd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a fault, disgrace, or vice to be remote from someone and not attach to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative construction with عَنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To glory or boast by reason of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use of having something behind or supporting one's status.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fat as a result of eating something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic expression concerning the effect of food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To know a text, especially the Quran, by heart and recite it from memory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of having something on one's back or at one's command.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold a person's need in contempt or treat it as unimportant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Literally, to put the need behind one's back and pay it no attention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike, hit, or hurt someone's back.
To suffer a complaint or pain in the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal form describing a person afflicted in the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become strong in the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a camel, and of physical strength located in the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To face a garment or provide it with an outer covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The covering is the exterior layer, contrasted with the lining.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put one garment, coat of mail, or sandal over another, or to layer coverings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional clothing and armor construction; it can also describe placing coverings one over another on an animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To elevate someone or make him publicly known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A disputed or dialectal construction in the lexical evidence, with differing explanations between elevation and public announcement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone know, discover, or become acquainted with something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative construction with عَلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat one another with hostility or to turn one's back on one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attested contrary reciprocal use, explained as each party turning away from the other; it is distinct from mutual assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek aid or assistance through someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually construed with بِهِ or عَلَيْهِ; wealth, for example, may be used as support against calamities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put something behind one's back for protection or security.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use of the back as a support or safeguard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare a camel or other riding animal for future need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prepared animal is kept in reserve for a journey or for replacing an animal that fails.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use precaution, secure oneself, or adopt the safest course in pursuing something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes taking additional measures to ensure ritual purity or success in an undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A household or responsibility to be maintained, conceived as a light or heavy burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expressions خَفِيفُ الظَّهْرِ and ثَقِيلُ الظَّهْرِ, referring respectively to a small or large household.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What is behind someone, especially in the idiom of stealing or acting wrongfully with respect to what is behind him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative rearward construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Adversaries who approach from behind, unexpectedly or without being known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in warfare or conflict.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill someone unexpectedly or assassinate him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom synonymous with killing by stealth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person regarded as outside one's group, disregarded, or held in contempt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative kinship expression for someone given no relational consideration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distantly related on the father's side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with close or near kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recede, retire, or retreat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dwell among a people, in their midst or main body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Originally conveys being surrounded and supported by people on either side; later it can simply mean residing among them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: During the day or within an interval between times or days.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Several idioms use the dual form for a daytime interval or a period between specified temporal boundaries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn something over and over, or to consider and manage an affair thoroughly and with foresight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The literal image is turning back to belly; the extended use applies to careful deliberation or management.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The outward wording, reading, or apparent interpretation of a text, contrasted with its inward meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In discussion of a Quranic verse's ظَهْر and بَطْن, the outward expression may be contrasted with interpretation, understanding, teaching, or esoteric meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A riding or burden-bearing camel, or the riding animals used for travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, عَلَى ظَهْرٍ can mean being prepared or determined for travel as though already mounted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property consisting of riding or burden-bearing animals, and by extension substantial property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from animals that support and carry a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The short or outer side of a feather, especially the part used in feathering an arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with the longer inner side of the feather.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper or convex surface of the hand, foot, or tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical specialization contrasted with the palm, sole, or underside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A land route, especially when contrasted with a sea route.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of an open or exposed way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Elevated, rugged, or upper land, including the higher part of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with low, soft, or level ground; ظَاهِرَةٌ may denote elevated tracts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a valley to flow with rain originating in its own land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with a valley receiving rain from elsewhere.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundant benefit or good obtained from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension from productive or elevated land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something absent, hidden, or concealed from a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A less usual lexical sense opposed to what is present or visible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By memory, without consulting a book or other written aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes reciting a text or carrying the Quran on one's tongue or memory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: At another person's expense, or from resources left after one's own needs are met.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same family of expressions can mean living at another's expense or giving freely from manifest competence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old cooking pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom suggesting something cast behind the back because of its age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Midday, noon, or the time around the sun's decline from the meridian.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used for the midday prayer, with the word صلاة sometimes elided.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person suffering from a complaint or pain in the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of someone afflicted in the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tortoise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The goods, furnishings, or utensils of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can also be contrasted with the interior furnishings as the exterior portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundant property or cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extension from useful property that provides support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel kept in reserve for future need or to carry a burden when another camel fails.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal is prepared for riding or carrying but may remain unused until needed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper, thick pair of wings of a locust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The exterior or elevated part of a stony tract.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the upper or exposed part of a حرّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pain in the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal form distinct from the ordinary noun for the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong-backed, sound, or hard and strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a man or camel; the evidence also extends the adjective to strength generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel whose back is unusable or unsound because of sores, galls, or another defect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an attested contrary specialization to the sense of being strong-backed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost or outward-facing covering of a garment or carpet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with the lining or underside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wrestling maneuver that twists or throws an opponent down onto his back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A named method of seizing and bringing an opponent down.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular manner of compression or sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the wrestling maneuver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind a person's hands behind his back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَوْثَقَهُ الظُّهَارِيَّةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prominent eye that fills its cavity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use of ظَاهِرَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remote from someone and not attaching to him, said of a fault or disgrace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with عَنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The external state, circumstances, or outward character of a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with the inward state or disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's need being treated as an object of contempt or neglect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figuratively, the need is cast behind the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sheep, goats, or other animals that come to water at noon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural and watering-time expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exterior or higher locality, such as the outer or elevated parts of a city.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of communities or districts situated outside or above the central lowland area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The coming of camels, sheep, or goats to water at noon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A recurring watering schedule, including watering on alternate days for some animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of ascent, an elevated grade, rank, station, or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can be used figuratively for an exalted station, including Paradise in poetic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made apparent; in grammatical terminology, explicit rather than concealed or pronominal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical grammatical use is opposed to مُضْمَرٌ and ضَمِيرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One possessing camels for riding or carrying goods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel made to sweat by the intense midday heat, or a person arriving at midday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records variant forms and usage around ظَهِيرَة and ظُهْر.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The conventional back-of-mother formula is covered by the Quranic zihar sense.
The upper or apparent surface of sky and wall is covered by the Quran-attested surface sense.

cautions: With عَلَى, Form I ظَهَرَ can mean becoming acquainted with, prevailing over, or mounting/surmounting; the object and construction determine the sense.

Some Quranic translations of the appearance and predominance senses overlap; the artifact keeps causative manifestation, dominance, and temporal noon uses distinct where the lexical evidence supports them.
The Form VI verb also has an attested Classical Arabic contrary use meaning to turn one's back on one another; that specialization is kept outside the Quranic mutual-support sense.
